subject: general
question: Gyaneshwar (1275 A.D.) holds a unique position in Marathi literature, primarily because he was:

options.text: the first and foremost Bhakti poet

solution:
The correct answer is __**the first and foremost Bhakti poet**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Gyaneshwar (born in 1275 A.D.)** was a prominent figure in **Marathi literature**. He is considered one of the most influential and revered Bhakti poets in Indian history.
 
• He is best known for his **Bhakti movement contributions**, focusing on devotion (Bhakti) as a means to achieve spiritual enlightenment and unity with God. *Hence, statement 1 is correct.*
 
• His works, such as the **"Dnyaneshwari"** (a commentary on the Bhagavad Gita), played a vital role in popularizing spiritual knowledge in the **Marathi language**.
 
• Gyaneshwar's writings emphasized the importance of **devotion**, simplicity, and universal brotherhood, which resonated with the masses and helped spread the Bhakti movement. *Hence, statement 1 is correct.*
 
• He was not a **court historian, playwright, or compiler of ancient texts**. His focus was entirely on religious and spiritual themes. *Statements 2, 3, and 4 are incorrect.*
 
• The Bhakti movement, championed by figures like Gyaneshwar, had a profound impact on Indian society, promoting equality and devotion over ritualism.
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is the first and foremost Bhakti poet.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **About Gyaneshwar:**

 
 
• **Gyaneshwar** was born in **1275 A.D.** in **Maharashtra**. He was deeply influenced by the teachings of his family and the spiritual environment of his time.
 
• He authored the **"Dnyaneshwari"**, a Marathi commentary on the **Bhagavad Gita**, making spiritual knowledge accessible to the common people.
 
• His works reflect his deep understanding of **Vedanta, Bhakti, and spiritual philosophy**, emphasizing equality and devotion.
 
 
 
• **The Bhakti Movement:**
 
 
• The **Bhakti movement** emerged in India as a spiritual and social reform movement, advocating devotion to God as the path to salvation.
 
• **Key figures** of the movement include **Gyaneshwar, Kabir, Mirabai, Tulsidas, and Chaitanya Mahaprabhu**.
 
• It rejected ritualism and caste distinctions, promoting universal brotherhood and spiritual equality.
 
• The movement contributed significantly to the development of regional languages like **Marathi, Hindi, Bengali, and Tamil**, as saints often composed their works in local languages.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Impact of Gyaneshwar:**

 
 
• He was instrumental in shaping the spiritual and literary landscape of **Maharashtra**. His works continue to inspire people even today.
 
• The **Dnyaneshwari** is revered as one of the finest spiritual texts in **Marathi literature**.
 
• His teachings emphasized **selfless devotion, equality, and the realization of God** as the ultimate truth.
 
 
 
• **Relevance of the Bhakti Movement:**
 
 
• The movement helped bridge gaps between **different religious communities** and fostered a spirit of tolerance and harmony.
 
• It profoundly influenced Indian literature, culture, and spiritual practices, promoting regional languages and devotional music.
